bug_semantics: HandlerMethod tries to associate a concrete @Controller data-fetcher method with declarations in its generic interfaces so that interface parameter annotations are merged into the concrete method. Its fallback override check compared each concrete parameter Class by identity with ResolvableType.forMethodParameter(...).resolve(). In a generic interface hierarchy, bridge erasure or an incompletely resolved type can make resolve() fail to yield the raw Class that the concrete method exposes; the candidate interface method is then rejected and its annotations are omitted. Under the vendor's stated conditions (Spring Security, @EnableMethodSecurity, and @Controller classes in type hierarchies), the missed annotation detection can cause authorization annotations to be ignored at runtime and allow unauthorized access to protected GraphQL data fetchers.
flaw_origin: Commit a1165051eb53890269df33ccec402b36646e07cf added interface parameter-annotation propagation and introduced isOverrideFor(Method), including the flawed ResolvableType.resolve() Class-identity comparison. Its immediate parent a7a78d9c6ccc02880cdfdf1cbde896a0035bcd76 contains none of getInterfaceParameterAnnotations, isOverrideFor, or that comparison. The later one-line production fix changes resolve() to toClass(), which returns the raw erased Class for matching.

evidence: Vendor advisory https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-41856 states that annotation detection can fail for @Controller data fetchers in type hierarchies, that security annotations can then be ignored with Spring Security and @EnableMethodSecurity, and lists OSS fixes 2.0.4 and 1.4.6.
CVE.org record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-41856 is PUBLISHED (VMware/Spring CNA) and describes unauthorized access to protected GraphQL data fetchers; it is not rejected or withdrawn.
GitHub reviewed advisory https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-phxq-526m-79px has withdrawn_at=null and directly references fix commit 63a89ed1379be646822dca9779b15dbf2ce45839.

git show 63a89ed1379be646822dca9779b15dbf2ce45839 changes HandlerMethod.java's fallback comparison from ResolvableType.forMethodParameter(candidate, i, this.method.getDeclaringClass()).resolve() to .toClass(); its regression test exercises generic-interface annotation discovery and bridge-erased Long/Object parameters.

GitHub issue https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-graphql/issues/1469 describes the concrete failure: @Argument annotations on generic-interface handler parameters are ignored because HandlerMethod fails to match erased bridge types; the direct fix message closes gh-1469.

reasoning: The public vendor/CVE/GHSA sources establish a real, published annotation-detection vulnerability and the attack preconditions, so FALSE_POSITIVE is inapplicable. Starting from the advisory's direct fix, the production hunk identifies the faulty mechanism: generic interface methods are rejected when resolve() does not match the concrete erased parameter Class, preventing interface annotations from being merged. Line history and -S trace that exact comparison to a1165051eb53890269df33ccec402b36646e07cf, and direct inspection proves the entire matching path absent in its immediate parent. This is the smallest public commit that wrote the fix-targeted flawed mechanism; it is a normal single-parent commit, not a move, revert, release aggregate, or decomposable squash. Tag topology places it in the maintained vulnerable lines and places the direct/main fix and equivalent 1.4.x fix exactly across the published patched boundaries. The BIC commit object has human author/committer identity and no AI marker, so BIC-only attribution yields NOT_AI regardless of the manifest's unrelated repository-level AI-commit signal.
